sprintGoals.1: Deliver the audited MCP foundation and a synthetic Grafana demo that can be run locally.
sprintGoals.2: Complete bounded Grafana reads and public uptime status reads with replay evidence.

milestones.name: Audited MCP foundation
milestones.goal: Start a local, read-only MCP server with strict configuration, redacted audited results, and a green build gate.

stories.title: As an operator, I can start the server with validated private configuration so that unsafe settings fail before a tool runs
criteria: Strict config and file-mode tests reject missing, malformed, or exposed credentials.
Startup permission tests refuse credentials with write actions.
A stdio transport test proves the server opens no listening socket.

stories.title: As an operator, I can see what every tool examined so that an empty answer has context
criteria: Every tool returns through the central result path with an examined block and bounded output.
Schema, oversized-result, and out-of-bounds tests prove the contract, including zero results.

stories.title: As a security reviewer, I can trace redaction and refusal behavior so that sensitive data stays out of results and audit logs
criteria: Provider calls outside the method and endpoint allowlist fail before network access.
Synthetic identity, secret, injection, and refusal tests prove redaction and one audit entry per call.

stories.title: As a contributor, I can run the same quality gates locally and in CI so that each milestone has reviewable evidence
criteria: Lint, typecheck, tests, evals, guardrail traceability, and secret scanning pass locally.
CI, dependency, permission, and public documentation checks use synthetic data only.

stories.title: As a maintainer, I can track delivery in a public roadmap so that each change has a reviewable story and sprint outcome
criteria: The public Project links the repository and has Status, Priority, Size, Sprint, and Milestone fields with Board, Sprint, and Roadmap views.
Epics and stories have public acceptance criteria, guardrail IDs, points, priorities, and test targets; a pinned Definition of Done stays open.
Issue templates, Definition of Ready, and the sprint process document explain the working agreement without private identifiers.

milestones.name: Grafana observability and synthetic demo
milestones.goal: Read bounded dashboards, alerts, metrics, and logs through Grafana and prove them with a local synthetic stack.

stories.title: As a contributor, I can run a synthetic observability stack so that provider behavior is testable without live data
criteria: A local demo starts with synthetic metrics and logs and has a reproducible smoke command.
The smoke test proves a dashboard, metric result, and log result without external credentials.

stories.title: As an on-call engineer, I can find dashboards and alert states so that I can orient an investigation
criteria: Dashboard and alert reads use only allowlisted Grafana endpoints.
Replay tests cover empty responses, malformed upstream data, and examined metadata.

stories.title: As an on-call engineer, I can query bounded Prometheus windows so that I can inspect a signal without an expensive scan
criteria: Instant and range reads use Grafana data-source query with UTC windows, row caps, and a minimum step.
Replay and rejection tests cover series decoding and each query bound.

stories.title: As an on-call engineer, I can query Loki for a time window so that I can inspect relevant logs within a scan budget
criteria: A read-only index-stats preflight estimates scan size before the bounded Grafana data-source query.
Tests prove line, window, selector, and scan caps and preserve structured log-code matching.

milestones.name: Public uptime status
milestones.goal: Summarize public status-page monitors and incidents without exposing monitor configuration.

stories.title: As an on-call engineer, I can see public monitor health so that I can separate an outage from a data gap
criteria: Only public status-page JSON endpoints are queried.
Replay tests use the latest heartbeat and distinguish unknown from up or down.

stories.title: As an on-call engineer, I can read public incident summaries so that I can relate status changes to an investigation
criteria: Incident summaries preserve public status and timing in an examined result.
Tests cover absent and malformed incident data without claiming a healthy state.

stories.title: As a security reviewer, I can prove monitor details remain private so that the tool exposes only public status
criteria: Allowlist output fields omit monitor URLs, tags, and internal configuration.
A fixture with planted private-looking values proves none appear in results or audit data.

milestones.name: Bounded CloudWatch investigation
milestones.goal: Read metrics, alarms, and Logs Insights with explicit time and scan budgets.

stories.title: As an on-call engineer, I can read CloudWatch metric data so that I can compare service signals over a bounded window
criteria: Read-only credential preflight and API allowlists gate the provider.
Replay tests reject broad windows and return UTC examined metadata.

stories.title: As an on-call engineer, I can inspect alarm states so that I can identify active alerts
criteria: Alarm reads are paginated and capped with no write permission.
Replay tests cover active, empty, and truncated results and redact account identifiers.

stories.title: As an on-call engineer, I can run capped Logs Insights queries so that I can investigate errors without surprise scan cost
criteria: Log groups come from a config allowlist; start, poll, and stop stay within a one-hour window and scan cap.
Tests prove timeout cleanup, scan accounting, and refusal for an unlisted group or exceeded cap.

milestones.name: Read-only IAM investigation
milestones.goal: Explain identity and effective access through least-privilege read tools.

stories.title: As an on-call engineer, I can identify the active cloud principal so that access findings have an accountable context
criteria: STS identity is summarized without credential or account identifiers in public fixtures.
Tests verify the read-only allowlist and redacted examined result.

stories.title: As a security reviewer, I can inspect role trust summaries so that I can understand who may assume a role
criteria: Role listing and trust documents are bounded and summarized as data.
Replay tests cover pagination, malformed policy documents, and redaction.

stories.title: As a security reviewer, I can simulate access and review findings so that a permission answer is evidence based
criteria: Simulation and Access Analyzer reads accept only scoped inputs and read-only actions.
Tests cover denied, allowed, unknown, and truncated findings with cited inputs.

milestones.name: Read-only product analytics
milestones.goal: Inspect bounded analytics, error issues, and flag state without exposing event payloads.

stories.title: As an on-call engineer, I can run bounded read-only HogQL so that I can measure an incident without changing analytics data
criteria: Only read-only queries with row, time, and execution caps are accepted.
Parser and replay tests reject mutation forms and overly broad queries.

stories.title: As an on-call engineer, I can inspect an insight and error issue so that I can corroborate a production symptom
criteria: Configured project allowlists gate reads and expose only approved summary fields.
Replay tests cover missing items and redaction of planted identity values.

stories.title: As an on-call engineer, I can inspect a feature flag state so that I can understand rollout context
criteria: Read-only flag state is limited to configured projects and omits private targeting data.
Tests prove missing flags return unknown with examined context.

milestones.name: VPS status with optional SSH reads
milestones.goal: Read provider status and tightly allowlisted host diagnostics without shell passthrough.

stories.title: As an on-call engineer, I can inspect VPS state and resource use so that I can identify host pressure
criteria: Provider API calls use a read-scoped token and an endpoint allowlist.
Replay tests cover state, utilization, pagination, and empty responses.

stories.title: As an on-call engineer, I can inspect recent provider actions so that I can correlate maintenance with an incident
criteria: Recent actions are time-capped and returned as untrusted data through the GET allowlist.
Tests redact planted identifiers and preserve source timestamps.

stories.title: As a security reviewer, I can opt into fixed SSH diagnostics so that host reads never accept arbitrary shell input
criteria: SSH is off by default and accepts only named read commands with strict arguments; docs explain Docker group privilege.
Negative tests reject shell metacharacters, disallowed commands, and excessive log tails.

milestones.name: Incident correlation and guidance
milestones.goal: Combine cited provider evidence and user-supplied knowledge into safe triage resources and prompts.

stories.title: As an on-call engineer, I can view a cited incident timeline so that I can compare events across providers
criteria: Timeline entries are ordered, deduplicated, and cite exact source queries and UTC windows.
Synthetic cross-provider tests prove missing-source warnings and no invented events.

stories.title: As an operator, I can supply a system map and runbooks so that the assistant uses my own operational context
criteria: Resources load from explicit local paths with file-mode checks and bounded content.
Tests prove no stack knowledge is hardcoded and reject symlinks outside the configured directory.

stories.title: As an on-call engineer, I can use triage and review prompts so that investigations follow the same evidence discipline
criteria: Triage, postmortem, and maintenance prompts cite evidence and mark uncertainty.
Prompt tests preserve the untrusted-data notice and forbid calls to write tools.

milestones.name: Evaluations with positive controls
milestones.goal: Measure useful incident answers and prove guardrail tests fail when protections are removed.

stories.title: As a contributor, I can replay synthetic incident cases so that answer quality is reproducible
criteria: A versioned synthetic case set covers healthy, degraded, empty, and partial-provider investigations.
The evaluator records case counts and scoring rules without live data.

stories.title: As a security reviewer, I can run positive controls so that guardrail tests prove they detect regressions
criteria: Each scored guardrail has a deliberate mutation or equivalent positive control.
CI fails when a required control does not detect its injected violation.

stories.title: As a reader, I can see measured eval scores so that release claims match the recorded evidence
criteria: README scores include evaluator version, case count, and date.
Tests verify the published score source and make missing runs explicit.

milestones.name: Release polish and guarded demo restart
milestones.goal: Finish public documentation, demonstrate the server, and release only after the guarded demo write path is proven.

stories.title: As an operator, I can plan a demo container restart so that I can review its target and effect before a write
criteria: The write feature is off by default and only a named demo container may be planned.
Tests reject absent flag, non-allowlisted target, and server self-targeting.

stories.title: As an operator, I can confirm one demo restart so that a deliberate write is auditable and bounded
criteria: A single-use, two-minute token binds host, container, and nonce; reason and health before and after are recorded.
Negative tests cover replay, expiry, cooldown, deploy lock, and every refusal's audit entry.

stories.title: As a new contributor, I can follow permissions and demo documentation so that I can reproduce the public examples safely
criteria: README, provider permission guides, and an asciinema demo use synthetic identifiers only.
Secret scan and documentation review pass against the release candidate.

stories.title: As a maintainer, I can tag a production-ready release so that a stable revision has verifiable provenance
criteria: The release gate includes CI, evals, traceability, SBOM, dependency review, and a signed tag.
The first release is tagged v0.1.0 only after reviewed code reaches main.

milestones.name: Private agent usage analytics
milestones.goal: Summarize usage and trends from approved numeric fields without reading transcript content.

stories.title: As a maintainer, I can summarize agent usage by safe job label so that I can compare effort without exposing transcripts
criteria: The parser allowlists numeric usage fields and uses explicit job mappings or session hashes.
A planted synthetic secret and email never appear in output, logs, or events; a positive control fails without the allowlist.

stories.title: As a maintainer, I can compare usage trends so that I can detect week-over-week drift
criteria: Report and trend tools return structured JSON plus a readable table with tokens, duration, tool calls, cache rate, and p50/p95.
Cost is marked estimated with price-table date unless a billing source proves it.

stories.title: As a security reviewer, I can verify optional usage exports so that analytics never carry prompts or responses
criteria: Optional events carry numbers and safe labels only, with prompt and tool-detail export disabled.
Tests reject prompt properties and keep read, write-only metrics, and optional admin credentials separate.
